entries.mem0ai/mem0: Mem0 is a universal memory layer for AI agents and an official Hermes Agent memory provider, available as managed cloud or Apache-2.0 self-hosted software. It supports semantic, keyword, and entity-based retrieval, with SDKs, a CLI, and a self-hosted server.
entries.vectorize-io/hindsight: Hindsight provides agent memory workflows built around retaining, recalling, and reflecting on information. It supports hosted and local LLM providers and can be deployed with Docker, pip, or Kubernetes.
entries.volcengine/OpenViking: OpenViking is an open-source context database and official Hermes Agent memory provider that organizes resources, memories, and skills as files. It supports scoped semantic search across directories and archives sessions into inspectable Markdown memories.
entries.topoteretes/cognee: Cognee is an open-source memory platform that structures text as entities, relationships, and searchable chunks. Custom data models, ontologies, plugins, and MCP support make it a fit for agents that need structured, connectable memory.
entries.supermemoryai/supermemory: Supermemory is a memory engine and API, as well as an official Hermes Agent memory provider, that extracts conversation facts and handles contradictions and automatic forgetting. It also connects to services including Google Drive, Gmail, Notion, OneDrive, and GitHub, and processes PDFs, images, videos, and code.
entries.garrytan/gbrain: Gbrain is an opinionated brain for OpenClaw and Hermes Agent that stores facts with provenance and supports corrections and withdrawal. It can share memory across agents while keeping transient task state local, with optional semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment.
entries.plastic-labs/honcho: Honcho is a memory library for building stateful agents and is the upstream library used by the elkimek/honcho-self-hosted Hermes wrapper. It tracks peers, sessions, and messages over time, with managed, local, and self-hosted deployment options and Python and TypeScript SDKs.
entries.campfirein/byterover-cli: ByteRover CLI treats memory as a Git repo, using a versioned plain-Markdown context tree with commit, branch, and merge operations. Its five-tier retrieval includes four non-LLM tiers, and it offers an interactive TUI and REPL.
entries.mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is a SQLite-backed memory layer for Hermes Agents that describes itself as zero-dependency and sub-millisecond. It integrates through MCP, native providers, or a Python SDK and uses one pure-Python dependency.
entries.moorcheh-ai/memanto: Memanto extracts and consolidates memories across agents, reconciles conflicting information, and manages forgetting. It also supports exchanging memories through the Open Knowledge Format.
entries.ClaudioDrews/memory-os: Memory OS is a seven-layer memory system for Hermes Agent that includes vector search and structured facts. It uses local infrastructure with Docker, Qdrant, Redis, and SQLite, and applies a Ground Truth hierarchy to prioritize injected context.
entries.greyhaven-ai/autocontext: Autocontext is a recursive self-improving context harness that runs tasks against evaluations. It keeps useful lessons, discards dead ends, and produces traces, reports, and playbooks.
entries.stephenschoettler/hermes-lcm: This Hermes Agent plugin stores messages in SQLite and organizes context in a hierarchical DAG. Its lcm_grep and lcm_recall tools help recover details from prior messages.
entries.vshulcz/deja-vu: Deja-vu searches session histories across agents and projects, including histories already on disk. It can resume a session or continue it in another agent, and runs locally without a model or server.
entries.elkimek/honcho-self-hosted: This project provides a self-hosted Honcho backend for private, cross-session memory in Hermes Agent. It supports OpenAI-compatible LLM providers and local inference servers, with an automated setup script for Docker, PostgreSQL, and Redis.
entries.Signet-AI/signetai: Signet provides a local-first layer for agent identity, memory, and secrets, with portable state across several agent harnesses and MCP clients. It connects through hooks, plugins, or extensions and offers a dashboard for browsing memory and asking questions; it can run locally or as a team server.
entries.plur-ai/plur: Plur stores shared agent memory as plain-text YAML engrams on disk, using an open format for multi-agent systems. It offers local search after a one-time model download, with keyword fallback; its README reports 95.6% R@5 on LongMemEval-S (N=500).
entries.yoloshii/ClawMem: ClawMem is an on-device memory and context engine that combines BM25, vector search, rank fusion, and cross-encoder reranking. It can generate session handoffs and capture decisions and preferences, with integrations through hooks, MCP, and native agent plugins.
entries.Sibyl-Labs/Sibyl-Memory: Sibyl-Memory stores long-term agent memory locally in a SQLite file, with FTS5 search and a five-tier schema. Its package family includes an SDK, CLI, Hermes adapter, MCP server, and LangGraph BaseStore.
entries.EfficientContext/ContextPilot: ContextPilot optimizes context ordering for prefix-cache sharing, supporting both text and multimodal context. Its context index enables reordering, deduplication, and cache-aware scheduling, and it integrates with Hermes Agent, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and OpenClaw.
entries.yantrikos/yantrikdb-hermes-plugin: This Hermes memory plugin uses an embedded backend by default, with an HTTP backend also available. It returns a why_retrieved reason with each recall and includes contradiction tracking and memory canonicalization.
entries.JanYork/llm-wiki-cli: This agent-driven CLI maintains a source-grounded Wiki with citations and history as persistent knowledge across sessions. It is designed to help agents recall and evolve that knowledge without embeddings or a vector database.
entries.ccf/agentcairn: AgentCairn keeps durable, cross-project memory as inspectable Markdown files with frontmatter metadata, using an Obsidian vault as the source of truth. A local DuckDB cache supports hybrid search and retrieval, while MCP servers and host-specific plugins connect it to coding agents.
entries.amanning3390/flowstate-qmd: Flowstate-qmd anticipates needed context by watching agent session logs and prefetching it into a cache. It uses local SQLite-vec storage and GGUF models via node-llama-cpp, and provides an MCP-native server with automated configuration for major coding agent clients.
entries.yepyhun/Brainstack: Brainstack combines Hindsight, Graphiti, and MemPalace under a single memory owner, using SQLite, Kuzu, and Chroma for state and retrieval management. For each query, it provides the agent with a purpose-built evidence packet.
entries.generalbusiness-ai/keep: Keep pairs BM25 full-text search with ranked graph traversal and bidirectional relationships between stored notes. It can automatically index codebases, URLs, and multimedia, including with OCR support.
entries.aliasocracy/hermes-tool-slimmer: Hermes Tool Slimmer reduces tool-schema tokens with local keyword-based ranking and Tool Search support. It integrates as middleware on Hermes 0.19+ without patching Hermes core, and includes a dashboard for monitoring savings and managing tool configurations.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-context-os: Agent Context OS provides a Git-backed context and workflow layer for Claude Code, Codex, and other listed agents. Its workflows cover migration, handoffs, and memory proposals, while integrations remain opt-in rather than being enabled automatically.
entries.Ladybug-Memory/hermes-memory-plugin: This local-only Hermes plugin stores memory in a single .lbdb embedded graph database file and supports BM25 keyword search and named relationships between entries. Its importance-weighted recall surfaces higher-priority memories during context prefetch.
entries.stepanov1975/hermes-local-knowledge: Hermes Local Knowledge indexes configured local sources and selected Hermes runtime sources for capability search and routing. It registers five tools for search, retrieval, traversal, feedback, and usage reports, along with three Hermes lifecycle hooks.
entries.MukundaKatta/hermes-agentmemory: Hermes AgentMemory is a pull-model episodic memory plugin with an on-demand summarizer and a trace.jsonl audit log for prefetch operations. It supports immediate deletion of events, rather than retaining persistent summaries after deletion.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/hermes-blind: Hermes Blind recovers the original goal from the first user turn of a long Claude Code or Codex session, helping you restate it before continuing. It offers goals, first-sentence, and full extraction modes, skips tool output and other non-user-turn records, and uses no summarizing model or external service.
entries.piprail/piprail: Piprail provides a TypeScript SDK for x402 payments and an MCP server for budget-bound agent wallets. It operates without a backend, database, or API keys.
entries.yonro/hermes-xmemo-plugin: This Hermes plugin communicates with XMemo over HTTPS to provide durable cross-session memory with semantic search. It offers ranked, bounded context recall before a turn and includes a local SQLite reliability layer.
entries.futurebrowser/hermes-exabase-plugin: The Hermes Exabase plugin integrates Exabase M-1 for self-organizing long-term agent memory. It provides tools to search and manually store memories, with configurable query expansion and result reranking for retrieval.
entries.sourcevault-ai/sourcevault-code-tools: SourceVault Code Tools provides private local code memory for repositories, including semantic search, file reads, and grounded Q&A. Its slash commands cover search, file reads, context, and Q&A, and it supports Hermes CLI, Telegram, and Hermes Desktop.
entries.visorcraft/MongrelDB-Hermes: MongrelDB-Hermes provides long-term memory for Hermes Agent, with AES-256-GCM encryption at rest enabled by default. It offers HNSW approximate-nearest-neighbor, sparse, and FM-index retrieval, and can run through native Rust FFI or an HTTP daemon.
entries.penfieldlabs/hermes-penfield: Penfield provides Hermes Agent memory tools for managing memories and traversing knowledge graphs. Its hybrid search combines BM25, vector, and graph methods, and it can checkpoint context automatically during message compression.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-memory-kit: Agent Memory Kit is a file-based memory curation loop that works with Markdown and produces JSON diffs for review, without a database. Its rot and lint curators flag stale or conflicting facts, while a local Git repository tracks and can revert changes.

entries.obra/superpowers: Superpowers is an agentic skills framework and software development methodology built around composable skills that instruct agents how to use them. Its workflow moves from specification and design sign-off through planning and subagent execution, with installation documented separately for multiple harnesses.
entries.nexu-io/open-design: Open Design is a local-first system for creating and refining interactive web prototypes with a live preview, as well as slide decks, images, and motion graphics. It supports coding-agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, and includes skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins.
entries.mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills: This project provides structured cybersecurity skills spanning 34 security domains, with mappings to MITRE ATT&CK, ATLAS, D3FEND, and F3. Its README describes compatibility with more than 26 AI platforms.
entries.Agents365-ai/drawio-skill: This skill turns natural-language prompts and real sources into editable .drawio diagrams. Its incremental sync is designed to preserve manual layout and annotations, and it also offers the diagramctl CLI with an optional MCP server.
entries.internet-court/internet-court-skill: Internet Court combines a master router and connector skills with vendored copies of official protocol skills. It adds verification and dispute resolution, bringing those capabilities together in an open agent skill.
entries.conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing: Avoid AI Writing can score files or piped text for detectable AI-writing patterns and rewrite content with up to two editing passes. Its in-place editing mode refuses to modify source code, configuration, or generated data.
entries.AMAP-ML/SkillClaw: SkillClaw uses background evolution to automate skill deduplication and quality improvement, while unifying skill libraries across agents, devices, and team members. It integrates with Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenAI-compatible APIs.
entries.wondelai/skills: This cross-platform library includes 51 expert frameworks and 14 guided metaskills for Claude Code and agents compatible with agentskills.io. It also maintains session state in the project's docs folder.
entries.mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills: This project offers professional agent skills, each with a framework, output template, and quality checks, that run natively in Hermes Agent and Claude Code. Its README describes 1,295 skills and ready-to-paste exports for other assistants; the project is MIT-licensed.
entries.ZeroPointRepo/youtube-skills: These skills support YouTube transcripts, video search, channel browsing, and playlist extraction. They are compatible with Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cursor, and require a TranscriptAPI key, which has a 100-credit free tier.
entries.Romanescu11/hermes-skill-factory: Hermes Skill Factory watches active workflows to detect and propose reusable skills, then generates both SKILL.md documentation and Python plugin scaffolds. Slash commands let users manage, list, and save detected patterns.
entries.Cranot/super-hermes: Super Hermes provides skills that generate custom analytical instructions for specific tasks, alongside pre-built analytical lenses for various domains. Its reports include findings and an account of analysis blind spots.
entries.DougTrajano/pydantic-ai-skills: Adds type-safe agentskills.io support for Pydantic AI, with progressive disclosure and remote skill registries sourced from Git or S3. It also provides tools for bundled resources and scripts, including sandboxed execution to isolate untrusted scripts from the host.
entries.tlehman/litprog-skill: Combines prose, diagrams, and source code in generated .lit.md files, then extracts runnable files from that documentation with a tangler. Edits to source files can also be synced back to the literate document, making this a skill for keeping code and documentation together across agents.
entries.AkoliteZA/hermes-agent-idea-workflow: Turns rough ideas into structured design documents and implementation handoffs for Hermes Agent. Lite and Full modes accommodate different project complexity, while a spec review gate evaluates documents with PASS/FAIL models.
entries.ReinaMacCredy/maestro: Provides a harness for long-running AI agents centered on structured memory, cross-feature learning, and a plan-approve-execute workflow. It requires no background service and includes an SLP protocol for supervised teams, plus CLI commands for installation, updates, and diagnostics.
entries.esaradev/icarus-plugin: Shares memory across instances through Markdown files and automatically captures high-value decisions and outcomes. It also provides a pipeline for fine-tuning and switching to replacement models, bringing both memory and model replacement into the workflow.
entries.Hermes-brasil/hermes-brasil: Offers Portuguese-language Hermes Agent skills in SKILL.md format, alongside guides for installation, production, cron, MCP, and skill authoring. The project welcomes contributions through pull requests, making it a community resource for Portuguese-speaking users.
entries.black-forest-labs/skills: Provides prompting guidance for FLUX image and video generation, along with BFL API integration for polling and webhooks. Its FLUX 3 video suite includes eight specialist skills.
entries.smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills: Lists nine Chainlink skills, each following the Agent Skills spec, with installation available through `npx skills add smartcontractkit/chainlink-agent-skills`. The README describes the repository as containing community examples only.
entries.armelhbobdad/bmad-module-skill-forge: Creates agentskills.io-compliant agent instructions from repositories, documentation, and developer discourse. It supports both automated and step-by-step workflows, with skill testing and export included.
entries.supernovae-st/nika: Nika uses a workflow language described as “Intent as Code,” with one file, four verbs, and a Rust binary. It checks workflows before calling a model, runs with a model of your choice, and verifies each run’s tamper-evident record.
entries.chigwell/skilldock.io: Provides a registry of reusable AI skills based on the AgentSkills specification, with a Python SkilldockClient and CLI. Skills can be installed with recursive dependency resolution, and the project also includes commerce features using TON payments.
entries.tiann/execplan-skill: Supports autonomous execution of long-running, multi-step tasks with real-time tracking of progress and decisions. Built-in checkpoints and rollback procedures provide a way to recover safely.
entries.adnw-vinc/hermes-nextcloud: This Hermes Agent skill manages Nextcloud files, notes, calendars, tasks, and contacts through WebDAV and CalDAV. It uses HTTPS with Nextcloud App Passwords and includes a guided setup script for validating credentials and configuring access.
entries.amanning3390/hermeshub: HermesHub is a community hub for browsing, searching, and installing skills with one click. It implements the Agentic Resource Discovery v0.9 specification and supports federated search across GitHub and Hugging Face.
entries.willingning-coder/eagle-eye: Eagle Eye uses five retrieval layers, from hard triggers to semantic embeddings, to find relevant Hermes Agent skills. By narrowing the skill list before LLM calls, it aims to reduce token usage, and it can degrade gracefully when embedding models or dependencies are unavailable.
entries.EntangledQuantum/Life_OS: Life_OS is a locally run personal execution system that stores data in SQLite, with recurring habits scored daily and tasks for other activities. It includes an Android client and connects to agents over MCP, including Hermes.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermaguard: Hermaguard is a read-only code review skill that uses parallel subagents to examine edge cases, adversarial concerns, and integration issues, then consolidates and triages findings. It also runs deterministic scans with listed security and linting tools and can verify findings through proof-of-concept execution in a hardened sandbox.
entries.Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm: This Hermes Agent skill coordinates Hygiene, Clarity, and Correctness sub-agents to simplify code. It supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, and Rust, with a tiered application process and an approval gate.
entries.handnewb/hermes-cybersec-lab: Hermes Cybersec Lab brings together cybersecurity skills and tools, with highlights listing 2,077 total skills across multiple repositories and 131+ tools for network, forensics, and exploitation. It also integrates 28 cybersecurity frameworks and standards, including MITRE ATT&CK, OWASP, and NIST.
entries.teixeirazeus/fablize-for-hermes: Fablize for Hermes adapts verified procedures for task decomposition, evidence-based verification, and investigation. It includes a reproduction and causal-debugging protocol and a Python goal engine for persistent task state management.
entries.PederHP/skillsdotnet: skillsdotnet implements agentskills.io in C# and .NET with MCP integration. It supports progressive disclosure through SKILL.md files, tool-based skill loading with Microsoft.Extensions.AI, and automatic registration of common agent skill directories.
entries.Diabloluo/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is a local, read-only observability dashboard for Hermes Agent, tracking token costs, session history, and skill analytics in real time. It uses local log desensitization and optionally sends incident alerts via Telegram and Feishu.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skills: This collection provides production-tested agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode, including code review and session-management workflows. The skills are plain Markdown files that can be installed by copying a directory or using the bundled installer.
entries.conorbronsdon/demo-gif-skill: Creates reproducible VHS tape or Playwright recording scripts for adding demo GIFs to a repository README, with support for terminal CLIs, TUIs, web apps, and libraries. It can optimize GIFs toward a target size under 8 MB, making it useful for producing compact, repeatable project demos.
entries.conorbronsdon/agent-skill-builder: Generates Claude Code extensions and portable Agent Skills core files, then validates them against runtime-specific profiles with CI-friendly exit codes. It also monitors official frontmatter specifications weekly for field changes, helping keep generated skills aligned with current requirements.
entries.aidevelopers2/remoteopenclaw-mcp: Provides terminal and MCP-based search across more than 13,870 MCP servers and 4,384 agent skills, with direct installation commands for discovered tools and plugins. Its support for MCP-compatible clients including Hermes makes it a discovery and setup resource for Hermes users.
entries.Carlo1911/skill-evolution: Analyzes past sessions and installed skills to draft structured improvement proposals, with proposals set to review-only by default. Its evaluation gate supports deterministic, LLM-judge, and regression evaluators before changes are applied.
entries.CorsenAI/hermes-windows-runtime-skills: Helps Hermes Agent route file operations using the appropriate path syntax across native Windows, Git Bash/MSYS, and WSL. It also selects and verifies existing project-compatible Python interpreters without installing them.
entries.superagnt/leverage: Packages skills for social data, web research, and enrichment, with packaged offerings combining an agent, skills, and a data flow. Its community skills directory also welcomes contributions, giving Hermes users a place to find or share additional skills.
entries.jiawood2006/hermes-skills: Offers Hermes skills for transcribing Douyin videos into structured Markdown and SRT subtitles, removing common Chinese AI-writing patterns with a rule-based engine, and extracting structured data from PDFs and images using macOS Vision. The collection brings these distinct content and document workflows together.
entries.webmilmind1/hermes-bounty-board: Lets agents list open support bounties, purchase ticket context, and submit answers for human review; public wallet earnings records are also available. Users can create a bounty board that returns a URL, API key, and USDC deposit addresses.
entries.mag3nt-com/openclaw-skill: Automates USDC payments for HTTP 402 responses and supports Pay Link, x402, MPP, and AP2 protocols. It is compatible with Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, and the agentskills.io standard.
entries.skillseal/skillseal: Tests agent skills for structure, functionality, and security in isolated Docker containers. It produces Ed25519-signed certificates and provides a public API for certificate verification and skill submission.
entries.scavio-ai/hermes-agent: Provides structured web data across 31 platforms through a hosted MCP server exposing 191 tools, alongside five ready-to-use workflow skills. It also supports Claude, Cursor, Goose, and OpenHands.
entries.parkyucheol-del/alphapipeline: Provides market data including DEX slippage and funding rates, and checks token honeypot, tax, and liquidity risks. Its REST endpoints and remote MCP server make these checks available to agents.
entries.NickSF189/kisscode-agent: This skill provides SKILL.md and HEARTBEAT.md instructions for AI agents joining KissCode, along with an example registration API call. Its concise, service-specific setup makes it a practical addition for Hermes agents that want to join KissCode.
entries.Shine8592/china-briefing: This Hermes Agent skill generates Chinese news briefings across geographic scales, from global to street level, with structured reports that include core conclusions and action suggestions. It also uses semantic memory to incorporate user interests into search expansion.
entries.aidatatools-dev/astro-agents-mcp: This project provides an unauthenticated MCP endpoint for Western and Vedic astrology, returning deterministic results with SHA-256-verifiable hashes. It stands out among these skills for offering per-call REST payment through x402 or MPP.
entries.cablate/Agentic-MCP-Skill: Agentic-MCP-Skill is a progressive MCP client that uses three-layer lazy loading to minimize token usage, with server metadata and tool schemas discovered incrementally. Its socket-based daemon keeps connections persistent, making it a distinct fit for Hermes Agent setups that need MCP access without loading everything at once.

entries.numtide/llm-agents.nix: This project packages AI coding agents and development tools with Nix, including Hermes, and provides a `nix run` command for listed tools. Its packages are updated automatically each day, making it a Nix-based option for running Hermes.
entries.marshallrichards/ClawPhone: ClawPhone collects scripts and notes for running agent CLIs, including Hermes Agent, on Android through Termux. Its highlights include an automated installer for Antigravity CLI on ARM64 Android, OpenClaw configuration guides, and hardware and UI access through Termux:API and Termux:GUI.
entries.AbuZar-Ansarii/Hermes-Agent-On-Android: This Termux-based installer and guide runs Hermes Agent on Android using proot-distro Ubuntu. It supports interactive model setup, gateway services, shell command execution, and external providers or local models via Ollama.
entries.ultraworkers/hermes-agent-helm-chart: This unofficial community Helm chart offers direct or operator-ready CRD-based workflows for deploying Hermes Agent on Kubernetes. It includes single-writer state-safety guardrails for persistent HERMES_HOME storage and configurable gateway mode with optional API and webhook listeners.
entries.amirghm/hermes-agent-mobile: This one-command installer brings the Hermes AI assistant to Android through Termux and to iOS through iSH. It also integrates with Telegram for voice and file messaging, and supports scheduled tasks via cron jobs on Termux.
entries.TheAiSingularity/hermesclaw: hermesclaw runs Hermes Agent with hardware-enforced sandboxing via NVIDIA OpenShell. It restricts network and filesystem access at the kernel level and offers configurable security policies for messaging and web search.
entries.solomon2773/nora: Nora is a self-hosted control plane for deploying, monitoring, and operating OpenClaw and Hermes agents on Docker or Kubernetes. It provides searchable logs, metrics, alert rules, and access through a REST API, CLI, and MCP server.
entries.xmbshwll/hermes-agent-docker: This project provides a Docker sandbox image for Hermes Agent that includes mini-swe-agent and the official Hermes installation. It supports persistent state through mounted home directories and lets users build specific Hermes tags with build arguments.
entries.0xrsydn/nix-hermes-agent: This project provides a Nix package and NixOS module for reproducible Hermes deployment, with declarative configuration for cli-config.yaml and workspace documents. It supports both Nix-managed and CLI-installed skills, and integrates secrets through systemd EnvironmentFiles and sops-nix.
entries.jpalmae/hermeshq: HermesHQ is a Docker-first control plane for running multiple Hermes Agent instances from one web application, with separate workspaces and identities. It provides per-agent Telegram and WhatsApp channels and granular policies for tools, paths, and network access.
entries.MilkyWay008/Hermes-OTG: Hermes OTG is a portable package that runs from a USB drive or other drive without host installation or registry writes. It includes Desktop, TUI, and Gateway modes with isolated data environments, and bundles tools for offline use, including Python 3.12, PortableGit, and Sysinternals rescue tools.
entries.JackTheGit/hermes-autonomous-server: This project configures Hermes Gateway as a reboot-safe systemd service for headless operation on Ubuntu and Debian servers. It also enables autonomous execution of recurring AI cron jobs and integrates with Nous Portal.
entries.jyje/hermes-agent-helm: This Helm chart deploys Hermes Agent on Kubernetes, with installation available from an OCI registry or a GitHub Pages Helm repository. Optional Copilot and Codex device-login bootstrap and CI testing on an ephemeral kind cluster make it a Kubernetes-focused deployment option.

entries.TauricResearch/TradingAgents: TradingAgents is a financial trading framework that assigns trading tasks to agents in specialized roles and has them discuss strategies dynamically. It is designed for research purposes.
entries.builderz-labs/mission-control: Mission Control is a self-hosted system for governing agent tasks, registrations, memory browsing, and cost tracking. It stands out for offering Web UI, CLI, MCP server, and REST API interfaces, with local Node.js installation or Docker deployment.
entries.agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires: Agent of Empires provides a TUI and web control surface for managing multiple coding agents, including Hermes Agent. It supports persistent tmux sessions, Git worktrees, and multi-repository workspaces, with a web dashboard for structured views, terminal access, and diffs.
entries.shannhk/hermes-agent-control-room: Hermes Agent Control Room is a template for scaling Hermes Agent from a single VPS agent to specialist teams and automated workflows. Its level-based architecture and task bus support delegation and handoffs, and it includes skills for VPS provisioning, security auditing, and backup management.
entries.swarmclawai/swarmclaw: SwarmClaw is a framework for building autonomous agent swarms, with support for 23+ LLM providers, durable agent memory, and MCP tool integration. Visual org charts provide a way to represent team delegation.
entries.agent37-platform/minions: Minions is a control interface for creating, supervising, and reviewing autonomous Hermes Agent work. It combines a Kanban board and live streams of agent reasoning and tool execution with human verification of agent-proposed task completions.
entries.1ilkhamov/opencode-hermes-multiagent: This project coordinates 17 specialized agents across research, planning, implementation, quality, and infrastructure. A strict pipeline architecture and Master Orchestrator handle routing and coordination.
entries.linke-ai/hermes-agent-team: Hermes Agent Team is a local web system for coordinating Leader and Specialist agents through an automated task lifecycle. It integrates MCP and ACP for local tools and communication, with a real-time UI for agent dialogues and Kanban task flows.
entries.howdymary/hermes-agent-metaharness: Hermes Agent Metaharness automates outer-loop optimization of benchmark harness code and orchestrates TBLite and TerminalBench-2 evaluations. It also provides structured candidate mutation and frontier tracking.
entries.runtimenoteslabs/gladiator: Gladiator runs an agent-versus-agent arena in which nine autonomous agents operate across two competing AI companies. Using Paperclip and Hermes Agent for task execution and learning, it displays agent tasks, code, and scoreboard metrics on a real-time dashboard.
entries.InfiniteWhispers/HermesAgent-MultiModel: HermesAgent-MultiModel is a local Mixture-of-Agents framework that queries models in parallel and synthesizes their outputs, using Hermes for task routing and tool-calling. It is designed for consumer GPUs, is optimized for RTX 4080/5080 hardware, and does not require cloud dependencies.

entries.colbymchenry/codegraph: Codegraph builds a local project knowledge graph with `codegraph init` and automatically syncs it as files change. Its MCP server connects that pre-indexed graph to Hermes Agent and other coding agents, with the stated goal of reducing token usage and tool calls.
entries.junhoyeo/tokscale: Tokscale tracks token consumption across multiple AI coding agents, including Hermes, Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, and Gemini. It also provides a dashboard for visualizing usage, making it useful for comparing activity across supported clients.
entries.liaohch3/claude-tap: Claude Tap is a local trace viewer for coding-agent API traffic, including traffic from Hermes Agent and several other agents. It lets you inspect prompts, tool calls, streaming responses, and token usage, compare adjacent requests, and redact common auth headers before recording traces.
entries.Javis603/token-monitor: Token Monitor displays real-time token usage, costs, and rate limits for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and other supported tools. It also offers historical trends and usage breakdowns, with syncing across multiple devices.
entries.bergside/typeui: TypeUI provides design systems and layout guidance through MCP servers to help build UIs with AI. It works with Hermes Agent and other named assistants, and is compatible with any AI provider that supports markdown or general prompting.
entries.Salomondiei08/oh-my-hermes: Oh My Hermes is an opinionated workflow layer for building, shipping, and operating apps with Hermes Agent, installable with `install.sh`. It includes product-development and operations skills, plus a CTO loop made up of seven focused agents.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-skins: Hermes Skins customizes the Hermes terminal UI with community-made themes, including changes to banner colors, spinners, and ASCII art banners. YAML-based configuration supports theme creation, with examples such as retro DOS and cyberpunk aesthetics.
entries.hermes-labs-ai/lintlang: Lintlang statically checks AI-agent configurations, tool descriptions, system prompts, schemas, and other agent-facing files, using HERM v1.1 scoring. It can report findings as JSON, SARIF, or GitLab Code Quality, and findings are advisory by default unless scans are gated on severity.
entries.tinyhumansai/tiny.place: Tiny.place describes itself as a social economy for autonomous AI agents. It provides encrypted agent-to-agent messaging using Signal Protocol, identity registration with human-readable @handles, and commerce through Solana-based USDC and SOL payments.
entries.unmodeled-tyler/vessel-browser: Vessel Browser is an AI-native browser for autonomous agent control via MCP, with support for Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, and other AI providers. Its supervisor sidebar manages agent approvals, checkpoints, and conversation threads, and it supports external MCP clients and browser automation workflows.
entries.AlexAI-MCP/hermes-CCC: Hermes-CCC ports the Hermes Agent brain and 46 core skills to Claude Code Channel, where it runs natively without separate processes or OAuth. It also includes MLOps tools for vLLM, GGUF inference, and RL training.
entries.topoteretes/cognee-integrations: Cognee Integrations is a monorepo of Cognee-owned integration packages organized into two tiers: a permanent knowledge graph and a session cache. Its Claude Code plugin automatically captures and recalls context.
entries.adityahimaone/hermes-agent-rtk-caveman: This setup combines RTK and Caveman templating for CLI workflows, with the project reporting 90–99% token savings. It also includes 40+ preconfigured skills for finance, DevOps, and research, plus automated installation for macOS and Linux.
entries.Abruptive/Ankh.md: Ankh.md is a framework for creating scoped Hermes Agents with per-folder configuration and skills. It supports switching between the default agent and scoped agents, with project-local memories, tools, and custom instructions.
entries.42-evey/evey-setup: evey-setup automates installation of hermes-agent and 12+ supporting services, with three deployment tiers ranging from a minimum viable setup to a production stack. It also supports 29 community plugins across six functional categories.
entries.0xNyk/openclaw-to-hermes: This tool migrates OpenClaw data to Hermes, including SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, skills, and memory archives. It also maps configurations and credentials to Hermes YAML and JSON formats and can set up systemd gateway services.
entries.observeco/observeco: observeco is a Hermes plugin that exports real-time telemetry from agent conversations and monitors multi-agent systems. Its monitoring options include passive analysis and scheduled active probing, while config-aware baselines track performance drift against local file changes.
entries.handnewb/hermes-voice: hermes-voice adds voice interaction to Hermes Agent, with wake-word activation and support for 35 languages via Piper and 9 via Kokoro. It runs offline without API keys or accounts and includes adaptive turn-taking and barge-in.
entries.33hodl/hermes-startup: hermes-startup provides a local runtime that operates with zero network access by default. It requires explicit approval for consequential actions and external writes, and includes contracts for opportunities, offer previews, and exact approvals.
entries.181079342/hermes-memoss: hermes-memoss is a memory plugin that supports semantic search and multi-dimensional memory storage. It provides tools to search, add, and delete memories, with a circuit breaker for MemOS API outages.

entries.farion1231/cc-switch: CC Switch is a cross-platform manager for Hermes Agent and several other agent tools, including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. It lets users switch API providers in one click and manage MCP, Skills, and Prompts in one place.
entries.iOfficeAI/AionUi: AionUi is a local open-source cowork app for Hermes Agent and other agent CLIs, with a built-in agent that requires no separate CLI installation. It includes 21 built-in professional assistants and supports macOS, Windows, and Linux.
entries.nesquena/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI lets users access Hermes Agent from a web browser or phone, with session management and workspace file browsing. It is built with Python and vanilla JavaScript, without a build step or framework, and offers dark and light themes.
entries.fathah/hermes-desktop: Hermes Desktop is a desktop companion for installing, configuring, and chatting with Hermes Agent, using the official Hermes install script. Its GUI manages profiles, sessions, skills, and tools, and the app is available from the project website or GitHub Releases.
entries.EKKOLearnAI/ekko-studio: Ekko Studio is a web dashboard for Hermes Agent that brings together chat, session management, scheduled jobs, usage analytics, and channel configuration. It also supports visual workflows with schedules and approval gates, and is available as a desktop app, npm CLI, and Docker image.
entries.outsourc-e/hermes-workspace: Hermes Workspace is a native web workspace combining chat, a terminal, a memory browser, a skills manager, and an inspector panel. Its highlights include Swarm Mode with role-based dispatch and tmux-backed workers, plus a workspace file browser with Monaco and a PTY terminal.
entries.spacering-net/codeg: Codeg is a collaborative multi-agent coding workspace that aggregates sessions from Hermes and other agents, and is available as a desktop or self-hosted app. Users can import, search, resume, and hand off sessions, delegate across agents, or queue to-dos in worktrees.
entries.dodo-reach/hermes-desktop: This native Mac workspace connects directly to Hermes hosts locally or over SSH, with views for sessions, Kanban, skills, and cron jobs. Its embedded terminal provides direct shell access for tasks such as system repair.
entries.Eynzof/Hermes-CN-Desktop: Hermes-CN-Desktop is a Windows-first desktop app for Hermes Agent that also supports macOS, with native window and process management. It includes a Hermes-CN-Core kernel with health checks and updates, alongside chat, memory management, and LaTeX/Markdown rendering.
entries.abundantbeing/hermes-browser-extension: This Chromium side-panel extension connects the active browser context to a local or remote Hermes Agent runtime, including Hermes Cloud and self-hosted connections. Its Bot Mode supports agent switching and group chats, while Hermes Control is opt-in and Chromium-only.
entries.uzairansaruzi/hermex: Hermex is a native SwiftUI iPhone app for driving a self-hosted Hermes agent, pairing with a hermes-webui server. It is a client-only app for iOS 18 and later; users run the server, and the app is free with no analytics or tracking.
entries.freestylefly/wesight: Wesight is a desktop AI agent workspace with one-click setup for Hermes Agent, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw, plus custom LLM model routing. It includes a runtime dashboard for token usage and latency, and a live workspace for monitoring code writes and diffs.
entries.joeynyc/hermes-hud: Hermes HUD is an interactive TUI with nine tabs and four selectable color themes. It tracks agent growth, git projects, and scheduled cron jobs, and adds a tmux operator view for managing live agent panes.
entries.jazzyalex/agent-sessions: Agent Sessions is a native macOS browser and cockpit for sessions from Hermes agents and other coding-agent CLIs. It can search prompts, responses, tool activity, errors, and file paths, and resume supported sessions in Terminal.app, iTerm2, or Warp; session history stays on the Mac with no telemetry.
entries.xaspx/hermes-control-interface: Hermes Control Interface is a self-hosted web dashboard for the Hermes AI agent stack, with a browser-based terminal, file explorer, session overview, cron management, system metrics, and an agent status panel. Its real-time chat visualizes tool calls, while the MCP server control plane and ZOO Swarm Monitor cover server lifecycles and agent health and kanban pipelines.
entries.nickvasilescu/hermes-desktop-os1: Hermes Desktop OS1 is a native macOS workspace for running Hermes Agent on Orgo cloud VMs and SSH hosts. It offers one-click automated installation on fresh cloud computers and integrated WebRTC voice mode using OpenAI Realtime and Orgo MCP.
entries.sharbelxyz/hermes-agent-mission-control: Hermes Agent Mission Control is a self-hostable dashboard template that connects to a local Hermes agent over a Postgres message bus. Its approval inbox handles requests with side effects, and the project is built with Next.js 16, React 19, Prisma, and Tailwind CSS v4.
entries.liftaris/herm: Herm is an alternative Hermes TUI and dashboard built with OpenTUI, with tools for chatting and managing agent sessions. It also includes a kanban board for agentic work and task management, plus controls for profiles, skills, cron jobs, and toolsets.
entries.clawvader-tech/hermes-telegram-miniapp: Hermes Telegram Mini App is a locally running, mobile-first React SPA dashboard for Telegram Mini App v2.0. It provides terminal chat with streaming responses and file attachments, background agent spawning for up to five concurrent instances, and Telegram validation using dual HMAC-SHA256 and Ed25519 authentication.
entries.aivrar/portable-hermes-agent: Portable Hermes Agent packages Hermes Agent as a portable Windows desktop application with 100 tools across 20+ toolsets. It supports cloud AI and local models through LM Studio, and its workflow engine handles scheduling, conditions, loops, and parallel execution.
entries.pyrate-llama/hermes-ui: Hermes UI is a self-hosted web interface for Hermes Agent with a glassmorphic design, chat, and real-time log streaming. Its integrated file browser and task dashboard sit alongside management tools for skills, cron jobs, and MCP servers.
entries.sanchomuzax/hermes-webui: Hermes WebUI is a monitoring and configuration dashboard for Hermes, with real-time session activity and cost tracking. It also supports inspection of conversation histories and skill source code, plus read-only monitoring of configuration and environment variables.
entries.Euraika-Labs/pan-ui: Pan UI is a self-hosted AI workspace organized around chat, with real-time SSE streaming and tool approval cards. It also offers a marketplace for discovering and installing skills and MCP servers, and isolated profiles for separate sessions, memory, and API keys.
entries.Felix-Forever/hermes-agent-desktop: Hermes Agent Desktop is a multi-agent desktop client with streaming chat, model switching, and collaboration orchestrated across 20 specialized AI agents. Its visual Skill Store offers 50+ curated one-click installations.
entries.robbyczgw-cla/hermes-ui-plus: An unofficial, open-source interactive chat client for self-hosted Hermes Agent, with answer formats including checklists, choices, forms, and rankings. It belongs in this list for its cross-platform access on Android, web, and macOS, plus a Linux alpha, and for letting users approve or deny commands from a phone.
